brief:
A group of nations will gather Friday to address what observers describe as a crisis in the international legal system, The Guardian reported. The meeting comes amid concerns that unilateral action by powerful states has undermined multilateral institutions and legal frameworks.

Participants view collective action as the necessary counterweight to what the report characterizes as unilateral pressure. The gathering reflects broader anxieties about the stability of institutions designed to govern relations between states.
dek: A group of nations will gather on Friday to address the crisis. The only response to unilateral bullying is collective action The international legal order is in shambles.
title: Nations convene to address erosion of international legal order
